hypothesis: The kitty-probe cold-start bottleneck (Kevin directive 2026-09-28): on silent (never-answering, non-kitty) terminals the kitty capability probe parks crossterm's process-global event-reader lock for its whole 250ms answer window, so keys typed in the first-mount window queue behind the lock and deliver at the settle (~250ms first-input latency). Code facts at b5bf28f1d: enable() is non-blocking for the render path (TTFF not gated); the residual cost is exactly the lock-hold; DA1-answering terminals already early-exit (KeyboardEnhancementFlagsFilter matches PrimaryDeviceAttributes too) so the full hold hits only silent ptys; TS is in-band (terminal.ts queryAndEnableKittyProtocol detects the reply in the stdin data handler; early keys deliver instantly) — the out-of-band lock-hold is a port divergence and the sliced window is TS-parity RESTORING.
approach: MEASURE FIRST, then the parity-safe cut. (1) Real-product flow (bench PTYSession, per-trial resident daemon, silent/DA1/kitty answer variants, keys at query+10..400ms, chunk-accurate ledger): the early-key visibility on the fresh-session flow is co-gated by the attach-snapshot paint (~250-450ms, arm-invariant) — the probe's marginal user-visible cost is the silent-vs-answered differential (pilot ~84ms at +50ms) plus the delivery-edge class. (2) SURGICAL PAIRED SUITE (the repo's own pty-e2e child mode: run_interactive against an instant mock supervisor — no worker spawn, the snapshot paints at mock speed, so key visibility == delivery + render inside the window): ABBA base,cand,cand,base x5 rounds over the two TEST binaries, unlink-then-copy sha-asserted swaps. THE CUT: vendored crossterm read_supports_keyboard_enhancement_raw v2 — the same 250ms window held in 10ms poll slices with yield between (deadline-capped; poll-error retries now also bounded — upstream retried without a bound); the query write, filters, DA1 early-exit, parked-keys contract, return values unchanged; pa-tui byte-untouched (probe contract, EXIT_RELEASE standdown, late window, byte orders preserved by construction). Candidates B (env-hint expansion) REJECTED with evidence: after the cut the window gates nothing user-visible (input delivers within a slice, TTFF never gated), so the only benefit class is gone while the misclassification risk (kitty behind env-stripping loses CSI-u) is real; the existing instant paths (kitty/ghostty/wezterm hints, dumb/linux) stand. Candidate C (adaptive early-exit) ALREADY PRESENT in crossterm (filter matches DA1) — verified live in the da1 rows.
parity_notes: Frozen surfaces: once-per-process probe contract (asserted: query count == 1 per child process in the new e2e); late-upgrade window semantics (the 150ms fallback/250ms cap unchanged — crossterm's return contract untouched); late-reply filtering (parser parking unchanged; replies never become user keys); the exit standdown + #3001 leak class (pa-tui untouched — the existing kitty_release_handoff_e2e and kitty_exit_routes_e2e are the oracles); bracketed-paste/modifyOtherKeys byte orders (enable()/disable() writes untouched); TUI output bytes (no render-path change; the probe's own writes move not at all — the query still precedes the first slice). Served-path assertions on every oracle class in the new kitty_early_typing_e2e: the query bytes must be on the wire (anti-vacuity vs env-hint short-circuit), the early key must RENDER (anti-vacuity vs non-delivery), the kitty answer must produce the flags push (upgrade class served), the DA1-only answer must produce NO flags push (early-exit class served). TS-parity anchors: terminal.ts queryAndEnableKittyProtocol (in-band reply detection, 150ms fallback timer) — the port keeps its documented divergences (no modifyOtherKeys arming) and the patch moves only the lock-hold shape.
